title: When Does Information Sharing Improve Decentralized Discovery? Aggregation, Independent Rescue, and Equilibrium Selection
abstract: arXiv:2609.01814v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Information sharing can improve a pooled estimate while eliminating independent rescue actions. This paper separates those effects in exact finite discovery models. A centralized action-budget profile shows that equal one-person accuracy can coexist with different portfolio values. Under a registered incremental-sharing protocol, a sharing step improves discovery exactly when pooled residual error contracts faster than an independent rescue attempt. Exact bounded registries exhibit compression, aggregation, neutral curves, and a bounded zero mixed class. In a two-agent Bayesian game with a hidden mixture of common and independent signal sources, the registered selected equilibrium yields a strict positive sharing interval at signal accuracy 3/5, while alternative equilibria show that the result is selection-dependent rather than universal. The models are synthetic and finite; no human or organizational data are used.

translated_title: 信息共享何时能改善去中心化发现？聚合、独立救援与均衡选择
translated_abstract: 信息共享可以在改进汇总估计的同时消除独立的救援行动。本文在精确的有限发现模型中将这两种效应分离开来。一个中心化的行动预算剖面表明，相同的单人准确率可以与不同的组合价值并存。在一个登记的增量共享协议下，当汇总残差误差的收缩速度快于一次独立救援尝试时，共享步骤恰好能改善发现效果。精确的有界登记表呈现出压缩、聚合、中性曲线以及一个有界的零混合类。在一个具有隐藏的公共与独立信号源混合的两智能体贝叶斯博弈中，登记选定的均衡在信号准确率为3/5时产生一个严格为正的共享区间，而其他备选均衡则表明该结果依赖于均衡选择而非普遍成立。这些模型是合成的且有限的；未使用任何人类或组织数据。
tldr: 本文在精确有限发现模型中分离了信息共享的聚合收益与消除独立救援的损失这两种效应，并证明共享何时能改善发现取决于均衡选择而非普遍成立。
en_tdlr: This paper disentangles the aggregation benefit of information sharing from the loss of independent rescue in exact finite discovery models, showing that when sharing improves discovery is equilibrium-selection-dependent rather than universal.
